description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of input and output token counts across four different context window sizes—2K, 4K, 8K, and 16K—in a study examining long-context large language models, as referenced in the paper “Shifting Long-Context LLMs Research from Input to Output.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number,” ranges from 0 to 120,000 in increments of 20,000, representing the total token count for each category. The horizontal axis groups the data by context size, with each group containing two bars: one for input tokens (solid fill) and one for output tokens (hatched fill), as indicated by the legend. For 2K context, input tokens total 9,320 (yellow solid bar) and output tokens 78,188 (yellow hatched bar). For 4K context, input tokens are 3,784 (orange solid bar) and output tokens 108,494 (orange hatched bar). For 8K context, input tokens are 1,401 (light blue solid bar) and output tokens 17,865 (light blue hatched bar). For 16K context, input tokens are 832 (dark blue solid bar) and output tokens 4,247 (dark blue hatched bar). The chart visually emphasizes that output token counts vastly exceed input token counts across all context sizes, with the 4K-output bar being the tallest at 108,494, while the 16K-input bar is the shortest at 832. The bars are not sorted by magnitude but grouped by context size, and the hatched pattern consistently denotes output tokens, reinforcing the paper’s focus on shifting attention from input to output in long-context LLM research.
